data.narrative:
Looking Glass, a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by Shawn Frayne, has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 private and public peers in Chips & Semiconductors, including public names (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and private contemporaries (SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, PsiQuantum, Etched, Tenstorrent).

Given the early stage and nascent peer set, only one triangulation method is reliable here. Stage-Progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $60M from the $30M raised baseline. A Peer-Median approach was inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-filter matches—while 11 same-sector peers exist, only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage comp survived relevance screening, falling short of the minimum three-point threshold needed to avoid spurious averaging.

The valuation analysis supports a range of $51M to $69M, with a median point of $60M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty: the 2.0x multiplier reflects typical but not prescriptive progression, and the absence of tighter peer triangulation means material valuation sensitivity to stage-specific financing dynamics and relative technical positioning within the semiconductor subsector remains unquantified.
